title: Family and representative survey
respondents: Family carers, relatives, friends, attorneys and deputies recorded in the People involved part of the care plan, where the person agrees or cannot give their views, answering in their own right
summary: The yearly February survey for families and representatives, alongside the annual survey: their own view of the care we give and how we work with them, labelled as family views and never merged with people's own answers. About 10 minutes.
purpose: Gives families' and representatives' own views of our care and of how we work with them, as the Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure requires alongside the annual satisfaction survey. Results are reported as family views and never merged with the scores of the people we support. It evidences Regulation 17(2)(e) (feedback from relevant persons and others) and people's experience for Responsive (Listening to and involving people; Providing information), Caring (Kindness, compassion and dignity) and Effective (How staff, teams and services work together). Questions about the person's care offer Don't know, because many families do not see visits; no question asks for information about the person that they have not agreed to share.

timing.when: Once a year, opening with the annual survey on the first working day of February for 4 weeks, with a reminder after 2 weeks

qualityStatements: How staff, teams and services work together

introduction:
{{organisation}} would like your own view of the care we give your family member and how we work with you. In this survey, "your family member" means the person we support, even if you are their friend or represent them. It takes about 10 minutes.

Taking part is up to you. What you say will never affect anyone's care. If you write the reference number from your letter, we can follow up your answers; if you leave it blank, we cannot reply to you.

This survey is not for urgent concerns. If you are worried about your family member's safety, or need help now, phone our office (out of hours, the on-call number in the care folder). In an emergency, call 999.
privacyNotice:
{{organisation}} uses your answers to improve our care and how we work with families. Our legal reason is our legitimate interest in running a good, safe service.

If you write your reference number, your answers are linked to you so we can follow them up; if you leave it blank, we will not know who you are unless you tell us. Your answers are seen only by our Registered Manager, Deputy Manager, safeguarding lead, Care Coordinators and the office staff who follow them up, never by care workers, and reports show combined family results only. If you tell us someone may be at risk of harm, we will tell our safeguarding lead and may tell the council.

We keep your answers for 3 years after the survey closes, under our Records Management and Retention Policy. We do not record the internet address or device you used. You can ask to see, correct or delete your information, or object to our using it, by contacting the office or our Data Protection Officer (details on our website). You can also complain to the Information Commission.

howToRun: The Deputy Manager runs it with the annual survey (SUR-PWS-003) under the Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure: each year publish a new copy of this template on the first working day of February with an end date 4 weeks later. CareFlow cannot send a survey to family members by name (only to people we support and staff), so this is a public form: send the link by email or text, or a letter with the link, a QR code and a paper copy with a prepaid envelope to the Deputy Manager, and offer to take answers by phone. Office staff who are not in the person's core care team enter paper and phone answers with Record response (channel Paper or Telephone) on the day they arrive.

Who to invite: everyone recorded in the People involved part of the care plan whom the person agrees we may contact about their care, and verified attorneys and deputies; where the person lacks capacity to decide who is involved, those named in the best interests decision, under the Confidentiality and Information Sharing Policy. One invitation per family member, even if they support two people. Never invite anyone whose contact the person has refused, anyone the safeguarding lead has restricted or who may be harming the person, a family member in an open safeguarding enquiry about the person, a family member whose complaint is at Stage 2 or with the Ombudsman (they get the after-complaint survey, SUR-FAM-005, later), or the family of a person who has died.

Give each family member a reference number on their letter and keep the list with the invitations: it is the only way to know who answered, because a public form cannot tell us. CareFlow cannot send reminders for a public form: after 2 weeks send one reminder letter or message to everyone invited who has not given a reference number in an answer. A family member is sent at most one family survey in any 4 weeks; event surveys (SUR-FAM-002, SUR-FAM-005) come first. A representative who also answers the annual survey for the person makes it one contact (library decision P10): the two surveys are linked in the library, so sent within 7 days of each other, neither holds the other back.

The letter, the link message and the phone script reveal nothing about the person beyond what People involved allows. By phone, read every answer choice aloud; ask the safety question only once the family member can talk privately, never in front of the person or another relative. Offer large print, translation or an interpreter to match the family member's own communication needs; many are older spouses, so offer phone completion and breaks.

Who may open individual answers: the Deputy Manager, the office staff who enter or follow up answers, and the Registered Manager. This is set in Who can see the answers: individual responses are limited to the Deputy Manager, the Registered Manager, Care Coordinators and the safeguarding lead, and results to the same staff, showing from 5 answers. Super Admin, Admin and the person who made the survey can always see both, so keep those roles to staff who may open them. Add the role of the office staff who enter or follow up answers. By default only managers and admins can record survey answers ("Record survey responses") and only managers can publish a survey ("Surveys", act): give these to the Deputy Manager and the office staff who enter paper and phone answers.
actingOnResults: Read every answer the working day it arrives and act under the alerts below, as far as the information allows where no reference number was given. Read every comment for safety, a missed visit or harm, even where the answers look fine.

How to count: report family views separately, never merged with the scores of the people we support; set them beside the annual survey's matching questions (on time, care workers they know, dignity, safe). For the frequency questions report the share answering Always or Usually, leaving out Don't know and Does not apply to me; for telling us, the share answering Yes, and I know how. Never report a group of fewer than 5 separately, and flag results resting on fewer than 10.

The Deputy Manager reports the results with the annual survey to the Directors and, in the May You said, we did summary, to family members as well as people we support, within 3 months of the survey closing, under the Governance and Quality Assurance Policy. Each family member whose feedback needs action is told within 5 working days what we will do. Keep answers for 3 years after the survey closes under the Records Management and Retention Policy.

alerts.when: "Do you feel your family member is safe with our care workers?" answered Sometimes, Rarely or Never, or any comment suggesting abuse, neglect or risk.
alerts.action: Tell the safeguarding lead the same working day; call 999 first if anyone is in immediate danger. The lead decides within 1 hour and refers the same working day where needed, under the Safeguarding Concerns: Reporting, Referral and Enquiry Procedure; someone outside the core care team speaks privately with the person. Nothing is discussed with the family member until the lead decides, because the person answering may be involved. A concern about staff follows the Managing Allegations Against Staff Procedure.

rule.task: Possible safeguarding concern raised by family

alerts.when: "Do you feel your family member is safe with our care workers?" answered Usually.
alerts.action: Where a reference number was given, the Care Coordinator contacts the family member within 5 working days to ask what would help, unless the comment needs the safeguarding route above.

rule.task: Family not fully sure person is safe: ask what would help

alerts.when: Any comment showing dissatisfaction that needs a response.
alerts.action: Record a complaint the same working day; it is graded within 1 working day and acknowledged within 3 working days, under the Complaints Policy and Procedure. What we share in reply follows the Confidentiality and Information Sharing Policy.

alerts.when: A missed visit, a medicines problem, a fall or harm described.
alerts.action: Log it in the incident log the same working day under the Incident Reporting, Investigation and Learning Policy, and the Missed, Late and Short Visits Procedure or the Medication Errors, Near Misses and Incidents Procedure where they apply.

alerts.when: On time, staying the agreed time, care workers they know, dignity or skills answered Rarely or Never, with a reference number.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator checks visit records and continuity within 5 working days and talks to the person we support first about any change, under the Person-Centred Care, Dignity and Respect Policy.

rule.task: Family reports care problems: check records

alerts.when: "Do we tell you what you need to know?" answered Rarely or Never, or a request for information.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator checks People involved; where the person has not agreed, they ask the person within 2 working days and reply only as agreed, under the Confidentiality and Information Sharing Policy.

rule.task: Family wants information: check consent first

alerts.when: A comment that the family carer is exhausted or not coping.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator calls within 2 working days (our recommendation) and tells them about their right to a carer's assessment. If the carer can no longer do their part, the Care Coordinator updates the missed-visit contingency and risk level that day and reviews the care plan with the person within 7 days, under the Needs Assessment and Care Planning Policy.

alerts.when: The overall question Poor or Very poor, or another low rating with no particular concern, with a reference number.
alerts.action: Tell the Care Coordinator the same working day; they contact the family member within 5 working days to agree what we will do.

rule.task: Family rated us poorly: agree what we will do

alerts.when: "Would you feel able to tell us?" answered No or Yes, but I am not sure how, with a reference number.
alerts.action: Send the complaints leaflet in the family member's format within 5 working days (our recommendation).

answers: Yes, but I am not sure how

alerts.action: Record it as a compliment the same working day and pass it on within 5 working days.

alerts.when: "Would you like someone to contact you about your answers?" answered Yes, with a reference number.
alerts.action: Office staff, never the core care team, contact the family member within 5 working days and record what was agreed.

rule.task: Asked to be contacted about their answers
